newsitem.title: UK: Major security alert causes chaos in London.
newsitem.headline: Major security alert causes chaos in London.

text.p: Five London railway stations and parts of Heathrow and Gatwick airports were closed on Monday in a major security alert that paralysed the heart of the British capital.
Police said the central London rail stations were evacuated and surrounding roads were closed after they had received a number of "threatening phone calls."
"A number of warnings have been received and we have evacuated these areas while we check them out," a police spokeswoman said.

It was not clear whether the warning carried the "codeword" normally associated with warnings from IRA guerrillas, who have stepped up their campaign against British rule in Northern Ireland in the runup to the May 1 national election.
King's Cross, Charing Cross, Paddington and St Pancras mainline stations were shut down as was the underground railway station at Baker Street.
Parts of Heathrow airport were closed off and the Gatwick airport train station was also shut as a result of the warnings, which coincided with Queen Elizabeth's 71st birthday.
Railtrack spokesman Roger Shire said: "This is causing massive disruption. It has been timed just as the morning rush hour is about to hit its peak."

Police warned people to avoid travelling to central London if possible. But hundreds of thousands of commuters were already stranded on trains, stuck in traffic jams or forced behind police barriers on the streets.
The alert followed two Irish Republic Army bomb explosions and a series of hoax calls on Friday which paralysed road and rail links in northern England.

Earlier this month the Grand National steeplechase -- one of Britain's biggest sporting events -- was abandoned because of an IRA hoax call to the racecourse minutes before the start. The race was eventually run two days later.

The attacks appear to be an attempt by the guerrillas to push the issue of Northern Ireland up the British election agenda. Peace talks, from which the IRA's political wing Sinn Fein were excluded, have been suspended during the election campaign.
